thread:
samir: opened PR to tighten Dedicated provisioning docs — added a short rollout checklist and an example of feature-flagging the new cooldown field. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1782 :clipboard:
caro: thanks — can you also show an example of how to toggle behavior at runtime (feature flag) for gradual rollout? ops teams ask for that specifically.
frank: adding a tiny feature-flag example and a CLI rollback command. keeping it short.
samir: perfect. also, make sure the SLA language explicitly distinguishes guaranteed reserved capacity vs best-effort burst. customers confused that paragraph before.
frank: updated: new sentence added under "Capacity guarantees" clarifying reserved pools are SLA-backed and bursts are best-effort but still respect isolation.
anya: posting the snippets here — feature flag example (yaml):
```yaml
feature_flags:
  dedicated_cooldown_v2: true  # rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100%
```
frank: CLI rollback example for infra automation if the new key breaks deploys:
```bash
redwood infra update-scale-policy --tenant t-99 --set cooldown_seconds=120 || redwood infra rollback-deploy --deploy-id $DEPLOY_ID
```
caro: can we include a short JSON migration script sample? infra teams love copy-paste.
frank: jq one-liner to transform old key `scaleCooldownMs` (ms) into `cooldown_seconds` (s):
```bash
jq '.cooldown_seconds = (.scaleCooldownMs / 1000 | floor) | del(.scaleCooldownMs)' policy.json > policy-migrated.json
```

samir: assigning reviewers @caro @anya. small ask from legal: call out that changing docs does not change runtime SLAs. adding changelog entry now.
ops: noted — will monitor support queue for tickets about preemption wording.
frank: small wording tweak pushed. merging after green CI. :shipit:
